title: add-exemplar-weighted-onboard-signatures-and-reader-links
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: We need stronger, compact provenance markers for newly onboarded models to improve changelog linking and targeted rollbacks. This PR introduces an exemplar-weighted signature for model metadata plus a small change to the release notes generator so that changelog entries include reader-friendly anchor links back to the model intake metadata and sample exemplars. Motivation: reduce ambiguity when multiple variants are onboarded in quick succession, make human and programmatic review of changes easier, and allow the console/CLI to deep-link into a specific exemplar that was used to generate the performance profile.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds exemplar_weighted_signature to the model intake manifest (compact 8-byte base64-URL safe signature derived from stable metadata + sampled exemplar hashes).
- Stamps the performance profile payload with the signature and a concise human label (e.g., "sig:wk7P3rA4,exemplar:short-uuid").
- Extends the changelog assembly pipeline to emit reader_links: a short URL fragment that the Console/Docs can translate to in-product anchors.
- Adds a lightweight verifier used during on-prem private installs to assert manifest integrity before accepting a model upload.
- Adds unit and small integration tests for signature generation and changelog-link rendering.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc: ENG-3214 (linked)
- [x] Implementation of signature generator and stamp in intake service
- [x] Release-note hook for reader_links in the changelog assembler
- [x] Tests (unit + integration in harness)
- [x] Console/Docs small mapping hook (UI change tracked separately)

Commits (high-level):
- feat(intake): compute exemplar_weighted_signature from manifest + exemplar hashes
- perf(profile): attach signature to profile payload and compact label formatter
- feat(changelog): add reader_link generation and embed anchor snippet in note body
- chore(tests): add deterministic test vectors for signature and link rendering
- fix(installer): tolerate legacy manifests without signature (backcompat shim)

Files/areas changed (high level):
- services/intake/src/signature.py (new)
- services/intake/tests/test_signature_vectors.py
- services/profile/serializer.py (stamp signature onto profile)
- services/changelog/assembler.py (reader_link generation)
- installer/onprem/validator.py (light verifier shim)
- docs/onboarding/anchors.md (doc brief for Console integration)

Backward compatibility: Manifests without the new field are still accepted. The verifier is opt-in via a config flag (onprem.require_signature=false by default) to avoid forcing immediate private installs to re-onboard. Changelog assembler will fall back to legacy anchors when signature missing.

Review notes / decisions:
- Signature is intentionally short (8 bytes -> base64url) to keep changelog and dashboard displays concise; threat model reviewed with Security (no secret derived from user data).
- Exemplar sampling uses deterministic reservoir seed derived from manifest timestamp to ensure repeatability across retries.

Review conversation (abridged):
- Ibrahim Noor: "Can we get a clearer migration path for older manifests? I don't want onprem customers to fail during upgrades."
  - Maya: "Added a config flag and fallback path; installer will log warnings and suggest re-ingest. See installer/onprem/validator.py shim."
- Sofia Patel: "Add a unit test that proves two different exemplar sets produce different signatures but identical manifests with same exemplars are stable."
  - Maya: "Added deterministic test vectors and CI check to guard regressions."
- Evan Ruiz: "Will the short signature collide often for high-volume model churn?"
  - Maya: "Collision analysis attached in ENG-3214, probability < 1e-12 per day at current onboarding rates; we also append a short exemplar id when collisions are detected at ingest time."

CI: Full pipeline passed after second iteration (flake fixes + added test vectors). Checks: lint ✅, unit tests ✅, integration (harness small subset) ✅, e2e staging smoke ✅.

Performance: negligible impact to intake latency (measured median +1.2 ms in a synthetic microbenchmark, 95th +2.8 ms). Signed profiles are ~48 bytes larger on average; changelog entries gain a ~32 char reader_link.

Release notes / user-facing impact: reader_links appear in the autogenerated changelog and Console will deep-link to the model intake page anchored at the exemplar. On-prem installs can opt into strict verification to enforce signed manifests.

Follow-ups (tracked separately):
- Console UX for clickable reader_links and anchor preview (PM-78)
- Rollout plan for enabling onprem.require_signature by default after 60d monitoring
- Add telemetry for reader_link clicks to aid debugging

Merge: Squash-merged after approvals from reviewers and CI green.
